acceptance: pi_rpc_session.rs gains `pub fn request(&mut self, command_type: &str, fields: serde_json::Value, timeout: Duration) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String>`: it sends the command via self.process.send, then reads records (NOT from `queued`; straight from the process, polling try_recv every 5ms like next_step) until a `response` record whose id equals the sent id arrives or the deadline passes. success:true -> Ok(the `data` field, or Value::Null when absent); success:false -> Err(the `error` text, or a fixed fallback string); timeout -> Err including the command type and the stderr tail; PiRpcRecord::Error(text) -> Err including the text
Every OTHER record read while waiting is pushed onto the BACK of self.queued in arrival order so a later next_step processes it (older queued items stay ahead of it). Nothing is dropped

If PiRpcRecord::Exited is read while waiting, set a new private field `exited: bool` on the session and return Err("pi child exited"-style message incl. stderr tail). next_step must, as its FIRST action (before popping `queued`), return PiStep::Exited once if that flag is set and then clear run_active/prompt_id as it already does for Exited; make sure the flag is cleared after reporting so Exited is reported exactly once. Add the field to the constructor

CONTEXT (all under crates/ajax-web/): pi_rpc_session.rs is src/adapters/web_session_acp/pi_rpc_session.rs. Its struct PiRpcSession has fields `session_id: String`, `queued: VecDeque<serde_json::Value>`, `process: PiRpcProcess`, `prompt_id: Option<String>`, `run_active: bool`, `ended_aborted: bool`. next_step(&mut self, timeout) pops `queued` FIRST, then reads `self.process.try_recv()` (polling every 5ms). PiRpcProcess API: `send(&mut self, command_type: &str, fields: serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String>` (returns the allocated command id), `try_recv(&self) -> Result<PiRpcRecord, std::sync::mpsc::TryRecvError>`, `stderr_tail(&self) -> String`. `enum PiRpcRecord { Record(Value), Error(String), Exited }` (Exited is delivered exactly once per process). Responses look like {"id":"..","type":"response","command":"..","success":true,"data":{..}} or {..,"success":false,"error":"text"}.

PI COMMAND SHAPES (from Pi's docs): `{"type":"set_model","provider":"opencode-go","modelId":"glm-5.2"}` -> response data = the full model object; failure e.g. success:false error "Model not found: x". `{"type":"set_thinking_level","level":"high"}` -> {"success":true} with no data. `{"type":"get_session_stats"}` -> data = {"sessionFile":..,"sessionId":..,"userMessages":1,"assistantMessages":1,"toolCalls":0,"toolResults":0,"totalMessages":3,"tokens":{"input":704,"output":3,"cacheRead":9655,"cacheWrite":0,"total":10362},"cost":0.0035091,"contextUsage":{"tokens":10362,"contextWindow":1000000,"percent":1.0362}}.
